title: Dairy Cattle Breeds: Jersey, Brown Swiss, and Holstein Friesian
text:
JERSEY
Origin: Jersey Island, France
Markings: light brown color
Desirable Characteristics:
✓ Breeding profoundness
✓ Longevity
✓ Milk best used for cheese
✓ Less susceptible to lameness
Performance:
✓ 400-450kg (smallest)
✓ 9,000kg milk/year
✓ Fat: 4.8%
✓ Protein: 3.7%

BROWN SWISS
Origin: Switzerland
Purpose: Milk and beef
Markings: Brown, light gray
Desirable Characteristics:
✓ Resist extreme solar radiation
✓ Quiet temperament and longevity
✓ Strength and hybrid vigor
Performance:
✓ 580-630kg
✓ 9,900kg milk/year
✓ Fat: 4.0%
✓ Protein: 3.5%

HOLSTEIN FRIESIAN
Origin: Netherlands
Markings: Black & white
Desirable Characteristics:
✓ Can adapt to different management and utilization system.
✓ Breeding profoundness
Undesirable traits:
✓ Not resistant to heat and susceptible to diseases.
Performance:
✓ 680-770kg (largest)
✓ 10,220kg milk/year
✓ Fat: 3.65%
✓ Protein: 3.2%

facts: Jersey cattle originate from Jersey Island, France.
Jersey cattle markings are light brown in color.
Desirable characteristics of Jersey cattle include breeding profoundness, longevity, milk best used for cheese, and being less susceptible to lameness.
Jersey cattle have an adult weight of 400-450 kg, making them the smallest among the listed breeds.
Jersey cattle produce approximately 9,000 kg of milk per year with 4.8% fat and 3.7% protein.
Brown Swiss cattle originate from Switzerland.
Brown Swiss cattle are a dual-purpose breed utilized for both milk and beef.
Brown Swiss markings are brown and light gray.
Desirable characteristics of Brown Swiss cattle include resistance to extreme solar radiation, quiet temperament, longevity, and strength and hybrid vigor.
Brown Swiss cattle have an adult weight of 580-630 kg.
Brown Swiss cattle produce approximately 9,900 kg of milk per year with 4.0% fat and 3.5% protein.
Holstein Friesian cattle originate from the Netherlands.
Holstein Friesian markings are black and white.
Desirable characteristics of Holstein Friesian include adaptability to different management and utilization systems and breeding profoundness.
Undesirable traits of Holstein Friesian include not being resistant to heat and being susceptible to diseases.
Holstein Friesian cattle weigh 680-770 kg, making them the largest among the listed breeds.
Holstein Friesian cattle produce approximately 10,220 kg of milk per year with 3.65% fat and 3.2% protein.
